description: Retention of converted existing residence to provide 1 no. 3 bedroom x 6-person maisonette, 2 no 1 Bedroom x 1 person flat, 1 no. x 1-person studio and cycle and refuse storage
decision_conditions: <p><span id="docs-internal-guid-ded3b428-7fff-1ce0-10de-879f756c3b22"><span style="font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">The development, by reason of a lack of provision of affordable housing, would fail to adequately contribute towards the provision of mixed and balanced communities and housing needs in the local area. As such, the development would not be consistent with Policies H4 and H5 of the London Plan (2021), Policies LP12 and LP13 of the LP33, and the Hackney </span><span style="font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">S106 Planning Contributions Supplementary Planning Document (2020)</span><span style="font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">.</span></span></p>

<p><span id="docs-internal-guid-b774c1a5-7fff-748d-b5d7-1de59822ebdb"><span style="font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">The development, by reason of the as-built lightwell occupying more than 50 per cent of the front garden area, with the lightwell not sufficiently set back from the edge of the pavement, the development would adversely detract from the character and appearance of the area. The development would, thus, conflict with Policies D1, D3 and D4 of the London Plan (2021), Policy LP1 (Design Quality and Local Character) of the LP33, and the guidance as contained within the Council’s </span><span style="font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">Residential Extensions and Alterations SPD.</span></span></p>

<p><span id="docs-internal-guid-1e612aa1-7fff-c901-13e8-078ab25a8bef"><span style="font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">By reason of the positioning of the cycle store and the subsequent loss of a central section of the front boundary walling, the cycle store would appear as an incongruous addition within the streetscene and would adversely compromise the integrity of the front boundary treatment. The development would, therefore, detract from the character and appearance of the area contrary to Policies D1, D3 and D4 of the London Plan (2021) and Policy LP1 (Design Quality and Local Character) of the LP33.</span></span></p>

<p><span id="docs-internal-guid-4b6ac415-7fff-15cf-1000-b7f92c596c1a"><span style="font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">In the absence of precise details having been provided, it has failed to be demonstrated that the cycle parking provision would provide a policy compliant level of cycle parking which would be safe, secure and accessible for all whilst also not opening onto the adjacent footway and compromising pedestrian safety. In the absence of precise details, the development would fail to provide cycle parking which would satisfy cycle parking standards and safeguard pedestrian safety contrary to Policy LP42 of the LP33.</span></span></p>

<p><span id="docs-internal-guid-304fb5ec-7fff-697b-39ae-43d5e7da3493"><span style="font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">In the absence of a Unilateral Undertaking or a Section 106 agreement securing appropriate mitigation by restricting future occupiers of the development from obtaining parking permits within the Controlled Parking Zone the development would likely exacerbate existing parking stress and congestion on the surrounding highway network. The application is, therefore, contrary to Policy LP45 of the Hackney Local Plan 2033 (2020) and Policy T6 of the London Plan (2021). </span></span></p>

<p><span id="docs-internal-guid-87db7b59-7fff-c3a0-91a5-76c1d326b666"><span style="font-size: 10.5pt; font-family: Arial, sans-serif; background-color: transparent; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline; white-space-collapse: preserve;">In the absence of a legal agreement securing the financial contribution towards carbon off-setting, the development would result in an unacceptable level of carbon dioxide emissions, contrary to Policy LP55 of the Hackney Local Plan 2033 (2020).</span></span></p>

<p><span id="docs-internal-guid-4b858cdc-7fff-ccb2-3f7e-468f9e6fd4c2"><span style="font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">The development, by reason of by reason of the floorspace of Unit 3 for a 1bedroom/2person dwelling failing to meet the minimum internal space standards in terms of floor area; and the level of light and outlook the basement level bedrooms of Unit 1 would receive. The development would, therefore, fail to provide high quality accommodation contrary to Policy D6 of the London Plan (2021), Policy LP17 of the Hackney Local Plan 2033 (2020), and the NDSS. </span></span></p>
